Kullback-Leibler divergence of an estimated Gaussian graphical model

Source: R/loss.R
kl_divergence.Rd

Computes the Kullback-Leibler divergence from the true zero-mean Gaussian \(N(0, \Sigma)\) to the estimated one \(N(0, \hat\Theta^{-1})\), $$KL = \frac{1}{2}\left[\mathrm{tr}(\Sigma\hat\Theta) - \log|\Sigma\hat\Theta| - p\right].$$ Twice this quantity is Stein's (entropy) loss of \(\hat\Theta\).

Usage

kl_divergence(theta_hat, sigma_true)

Arguments

theta_hat

Estimated p x p precision matrix.

sigma_true

True p x p covariance matrix.

Value

A non-negative number, or NA if \(\Sigma\hat\Theta\) has a non-positive determinant (e.g. theta_hat is not positive definite), the inputs have missing values, or the computation fails.

See also

relative_frobenius()

Examples

Sigma <- matrix(c(1, 0.5, 0.5, 1), 2, 2)
kl_divergence(solve(Sigma), Sigma)   # 0
#> [1] 0
kl_divergence(diag(2), Sigma)
#> [1] 0.143841
